description:
The HUD speed readout on the /fly page shows 'NaN km/s' for outer-planet destinations (Jupiter at 5.2 AU, Saturn at 9.5 AU, Uranus, Neptune, Pluto, and asteroids/dwarf planets beyond ~2.5 AU) for the entire mission duration. The velocity arrow also disappears (NaN × 0.4 → invisible).

Expected: The speed readout displays a valid finite number (km/s) for every mission destination at every point along the trajectory. The velocity arrow remains visible.

Acceptance criteria:
- heliocentricSpeed(rAu, aTransferAu) returns a non-NaN finite number for every rAu > 0 given aTransferAu = 1.262 AU (the existing Earth→Mars transfer a). In particular, for rAu = 5.2 (Jupiter), rAu = 9.5 (Saturn), and rAu = 30.1 (Neptune), the function must return finite values, not NaN. [code-invariant: NaN in a numeric HUD display is a crash-level invariant; Math.sqrt of a negative radicand produces NaN per IEEE 754]
- The specific NaN-producing condition is when r > 2a (r exceeding the transfer ellipse apohelion), which occurs on every outer-planet trajectory because the hardcoded a = 1.262 AU corresponds only to Earth→Mars. The fix must eliminate NaN from this condition without changing the a input value. [reporter: "The bug I reported is about the speed function's out-of-range behavior (NaN when radius exceeds apohelion)" and "Keep the inputs as they are"]

Domain facts:
- heliocentricSpeed in fly-physics.ts computes v = √(µ · (2/r − 1/a)) · AU/yr→km/s with no NaN guard
- visViva in orbital.ts is the raw formula with the same behavior — do not change visViva, it is correct for its bounded-orbit contract; fix the outer-layer function heliocentricSpeed that calls it with potentially out-of-range r
- a = (R_EARTH_AU + R_MARS_AU) / 2 ≈ 1.262 AU — the reporter instructs to keep this value unchanged

Target: src/lib/orbital/fly-physics.ts — heliocentricSpeed
Do NOT change src/routes/fly/+page.svelte — it is not the owner of this symptom.
